product.name: Tasky
product.summary: A small personal task manager that keeps everything in your browser
product.description: Tasky is the Orbit reference application: a deliberately small, real task manager with lists, due dates, Today and Overdue views, and local-only storage.

entities.name: Task Management
entities.summary: Create, edit, complete and delete personal tasks
entities.description: Everything a person does to keep their own to-do items up to date: capturing a task, changing its details, ticking it off and deleting it when it no longer matters.

entities.name: Lists
entities.summary: Create, rename and delete lists, and assign tasks to them
entities.description: Tasks always belong to exactly one list: the built-in Inbox or a custom list the person created.

entities.name: Task Discovery
entities.summary: Find the right tasks through Inbox, Today, All Tasks and lists
entities.description: Views that answer "what is in this list?", "what needs attention today?" and "what do I have in total?".

entities.name: Local Data
entities.summary: Everything Tasky stores, kept in this browser only
entities.description: One versioned document in browser localStorage holds lists and tasks. Nothing leaves the device and there are no accounts. The repositories below share this storage helper.

behaviors.name: Unreadable data is never overwritten
behaviors.expected: If the stored document is not valid JSON or fails validation, Tasky shows a banner offering "Download raw data" and "Start fresh", does not crash, and writes nothing until the person chooses.

behaviors.name: Starting fresh keeps a backup
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Start fresh" copies the unreadable raw text to a separate backup storage key before clearing the main key.

behaviors.name: Demo data only on request
behaviors.expected: Sample lists and tasks are written only after explicit "Load demo data" or confirmed "Reset demo data"; existing data is never reseeded, even when it is empty.

behaviors.name: Failed saves are reported
behaviors.expected: When the browser refuses a write (for example storage is full or blocked) the person sees an error message and the previously saved data is left intact.

entities.name: Task Repository
entities.summary: Reads and writes task records
entities.description: Validates and persists task changes (create, update, complete, delete) in the shared local document and stamps createdAt/updatedAt.

behaviors.name: Creating a task normalizes it
behaviors.expected: A created task gets a unique id, a trimmed title, Inbox as list unless one is given, completed=false and equal createdAt/updatedAt timestamps.

behaviors.name: Invalid input is rejected without writing
behaviors.expected: Blank titles, impossible calendar dates and unknown list ids raise a validation error and leave storage unchanged.

behaviors.name: Updates keep identity and refresh updatedAt
behaviors.expected: Updating or completing a task keeps its id and createdAt, advances updatedAt, and deleting removes only that task.

behaviors.name: Changes survive reload
behaviors.expected: Task changes are written to the versioned storage key immediately, so a new repository over the same storage (or a page reload) sees the same tasks.

entities.name: List Repository
entities.summary: Reads and writes custom list records
entities.description: Creates, renames and deletes custom lists; Inbox is virtual and never stored. Deleting a list rewrites its tasks to Inbox in the same write.

behaviors.name: List names are unique and non-blank
behaviors.expected: Creating or renaming a list with a blank name, a case-insensitive duplicate or the name "Inbox" is rejected; a valid rename keeps the list id.

behaviors.name: List deletion is atomic and lossless
behaviors.expected: Deleting a list removes it and reassigns each of its tasks to Inbox in a single write, reports how many tasks moved, and never deletes tasks.

entities.name: Presentation Logic
entities.summary: Pure rules that decide what the screens show
entities.description: Framework-free functions that turn stored data and the current local date into the ordered task lists and badges that the interface renders.

entities.name: Task Filtering and Sorting
entities.summary: Selects and orders tasks for each view
entities.description: Implements which tasks belong to Inbox, a custom list, Today and All Tasks, whether completed tasks are shown, and the one deterministic ordering used everywhere.

behaviors.name: Deterministic task ordering
behaviors.expected: Tasks are ordered incomplete first, then by due date ascending with undated tasks last, then by createdAt, then by id, independent of storage order.

behaviors.name: Today selection rule
behaviors.expected: The Today filter returns exactly the incomplete tasks with a due date on or before the supplied local date, from every list, in standard order.

behaviors.name: Completed tasks are hidden except where requested
behaviors.expected: Every view hides completed tasks unless showCompleted is set, except All Tasks, which always includes them after open tasks; sidebar counts include only open tasks.

entities.name: Local Date Evaluation
entities.summary: Works out today, overdue and day rollover from the local calendar
entities.description: Converts an injectable "now" into the user's local calendar date and answers whether a due date is today, overdue, or due later; also schedules re-evaluation at the next local midnight.

behaviors.name: Local calendar date, not UTC
behaviors.expected: The current date is read from the local year, month and day of the supplied instant, so late-evening and early-morning times map to the date shown on the wall clock.

behaviors.name: Overdue and due-today classification
behaviors.expected: A due date before the local date is overdue, a due date on or before it counts for Today, and a missing due date is neither.

behaviors.name: Day rollover re-evaluation
behaviors.expected: The delay to the next local midnight is computed exactly, and a due-today task is classified overdue once the local date advances.

entities.name: Create Task
entities.summary: Add a new task to Tasky with a title and optional details.
entities.description: A person captures a to-do item from the New task dialog. Only a title is required; notes, a due date and the list are optional, and the task lands in Inbox unless a custom list is being viewed.

behaviors.name: User can create a new task
behaviors.expected: Opening "New task", entering a title and choosing "Add task" adds the task to the list and closes the dialog.

behaviors.name: User can add notes and a due date when creating a task
behaviors.expected: The New task dialog accepts optional notes and a due date, and the task keeps both once added.

behaviors.name: User will find a new task in the list they are viewing
behaviors.expected: A task created while viewing a custom list is added to that list, and the List field is pre-filled with it.

behaviors.name: User will find a new task in Inbox when not viewing a custom list
behaviors.expected: A task created from Inbox, Today or All Tasks is added to Inbox, and the List field defaults to Inbox.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to add a task with a blank title
behaviors.expected: Submitting an empty or whitespace-only title shows "Enter a title for the task." beside the Title field, keeps the dialog open and adds nothing; the user can then enter a title and add the task.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to add a task with a title that is too long
behaviors.expected: A title longer than 200 characters shows "Keep the title under 200 characters." beside the Title field and adds nothing.

behaviors.name: User will see their task title saved without leading or trailing spaces
behaviors.expected: Spaces around the title are removed when the task is created.

behaviors.name: User can come back later and find the task they created
behaviors.expected: Created tasks are kept in the browser and are still present after reloading the page.

entities.name: Edit Task
entities.summary: Change the details of a task that already exists.
entities.description: A person reopens a task from its Edit control and updates its title, notes, due date or list in one accessible dialog.

behaviors.name: User can change the title, notes and due date of a task
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Edit '<task>'" opens the Edit task dialog with the current values; choosing "Save changes" updates the task in the list immediately and the new values show when it is reopened.

behaviors.name: User can move a task to a different list
behaviors.expected: Changing the List field in the Edit task dialog removes the task from its old list view and shows it in the new one.

behaviors.name: User can remove a task's due date
behaviors.expected: Clearing the Due date field and saving leaves the task with no due date.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to save a task with a blank title
behaviors.expected: Saving an edit with an empty or whitespace-only title shows an error beside the Title field, keeps the dialog open and leaves the task unchanged.

behaviors.name: User can edit a task using only the keyboard
behaviors.expected: The Edit task dialog moves focus to the Title field, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the dialog, closes on Escape and returns focus to the Edit control that opened it.

entities.name: Complete Task
entities.summary: Tick a task off, and reopen it if it was not really finished.
entities.description: Completing a task is a single, reversible action. Finished tasks leave the default views but can be shown again.

behaviors.name: User can mark a task complete
behaviors.expected: Ticking "Mark '<task>' complete" removes the task from the default list view.

behaviors.name: User can show completed tasks again
behaviors.expected: Switching on "Show completed" lists finished tasks after the open ones, marked as complete.

behaviors.name: User can reopen a completed task
behaviors.expected: Unticking "Mark '<task>' incomplete" returns the task to its list as an open task.

behaviors.name: User will not see completed tasks in Today
behaviors.expected: A completed task is hidden from Today, even if it is due today or overdue, unless "Show completed" is on.

behaviors.name: User can complete and reopen tasks using only the keyboard
behaviors.expected: Each task checkbox is named after its task ("Mark 'Buy milk' complete") and toggles with the Space key.

entities.name: Delete Task
entities.summary: Permanently remove a task after confirming.
entities.description: Deleting is permanent, so it always asks first and names the task being removed.

behaviors.name: User will be asked to confirm before a task is deleted
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Delete '<task>'" opens a "Delete task?" confirmation that names the task; nothing is removed yet.

behaviors.name: User can cancel a deletion and keep the task
behaviors.expected: Choosing Cancel closes the confirmation and leaves the task in its list untouched.

behaviors.name: User can permanently delete a task
behaviors.expected: Confirming with "Delete task" removes the task from every view and it cannot be restored.

behaviors.name: User can delete a task using only the keyboard
behaviors.expected: The Delete control is named after its task, opens the confirmation with Enter and puts keyboard focus on Cancel so a stray keypress cannot delete.

entities.name: Create List
entities.summary: Add a custom list to group related tasks.
entities.description: A person creates a list (e.g. Work, Errands) from the New list dialog. Names must contain visible text and be unique, and the new list opens straight away.

behaviors.name: User can create a new list
behaviors.expected: Choosing "New list", entering a name and choosing "Create list" adds the list to the sidebar and closes the dialog.

behaviors.name: User will be taken to the new list as soon as it is created
behaviors.expected: The new list opens with its name as the page heading and is highlighted as the current item in the sidebar.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to create a list with a blank name
behaviors.expected: Submitting an empty or whitespace-only name shows "Enter a name for the list." beside the List name field, keeps the dialog open and creates nothing.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to create a list with a name that is already used
behaviors.expected: A name matching another list, ignoring upper and lower case, shows "A list with that name already exists." and creates nothing.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to name a list "Inbox"
behaviors.expected: Using "Inbox" in any letter case shows "A list with that name already exists." because Inbox is reserved.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they try to create a list with a name that is too long
behaviors.expected: A name longer than 60 characters shows "Keep the name under 60 characters." and creates nothing.

entities.name: Rename List
entities.summary: Change the name of a custom list.
entities.description: A person renames a custom list from its list view. The built-in Inbox cannot be renamed.

behaviors.name: User can rename a list
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Rename list" opens a dialog pre-filled with the current name; choosing "Save name" updates the sidebar and the page heading immediately and the old name disappears.

behaviors.name: User will still see all of the list's tasks after renaming it
behaviors.expected: Renaming changes only the name; the list keeps its identity and every task in it.

behaviors.name: User will see an error message when they rename a list to a blank or already used name
behaviors.expected: A blank, whitespace-only or duplicate name (ignoring case) shows an inline message, keeps the dialog open and leaves the list name unchanged.

behaviors.name: User will not be offered a way to rename Inbox
behaviors.expected: The Inbox view has no "Rename list" control, while every custom list does; renaming Inbox programmatically is refused.

entities.name: Delete List
entities.summary: Remove a custom list without losing its tasks.
entities.description: Deleting a list always asks first, says how many tasks will move, and sends them to Inbox. The built-in Inbox cannot be deleted.

behaviors.name: User will be told how many tasks will move to Inbox before a list is deleted
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Delete list" opens a confirmation naming the list and stating, e.g., "3 tasks will be moved to Inbox, not deleted"; nothing is removed yet.

behaviors.name: User can cancel deleting a list and keep it
behaviors.expected: Choosing Cancel closes the confirmation and the list stays in the sidebar unchanged.

behaviors.name: User can delete a list
behaviors.expected: Confirming with "Delete list" removes the list from the sidebar and takes the user to Inbox.

behaviors.name: User will find every task from a deleted list in Inbox
behaviors.expected: Open and completed tasks of the deleted list move to Inbox and none are lost; tasks in other lists are not affected.

behaviors.name: User will not be offered a way to delete Inbox
behaviors.expected: The Inbox view has no "Delete list" control, while every custom list does; deleting Inbox programmatically is refused.

entities.name: Assign Task to List
entities.summary: Decide which list a task belongs to, by default and later.
entities.description: A new task lands in Inbox unless it is created while viewing a custom list. A task can be moved to another list at any time by editing it.

behaviors.name: User will find a new task in the custom list they are viewing
behaviors.expected: A task created inside a custom list is added to that list.

behaviors.name: User will find a new task in Inbox when they create it outside a custom list
behaviors.expected: A task created from Inbox, Today or All Tasks is added to Inbox.

behaviors.name: User can move a task to a different list
behaviors.expected: Changing the List field in the Edit task dialog removes the task from its old list view and shows it in the new list.

entities.name: Browse Inbox and Lists
entities.summary: See what is in Inbox or in a single custom list.
entities.description: Inbox and each custom list show only their own tasks, hide finished ones unless asked, and show how many open tasks they hold.

behaviors.name: User can see only the tasks in Inbox when they open Inbox
behaviors.expected: The Inbox view lists only tasks in Inbox, not tasks from custom lists.

behaviors.name: User can open a custom list and see only the tasks in that list
behaviors.expected: Selecting a list in the sidebar shows only that list's tasks under its name.

behaviors.name: User will not see completed tasks until they turn on "Show completed"
behaviors.expected: Inbox and custom lists hide completed tasks by default, and "Show completed" lists them after the open ones.

behaviors.name: User can see how many open tasks each list has in the sidebar
behaviors.expected: The sidebar count next to Inbox or a list equals its number of open tasks; completed tasks are not counted.

behaviors.name: User will see open tasks ordered by due date, with undated tasks last
behaviors.expected: Within a view, open tasks come first, earliest due date first, then tasks without a due date, in the order they were created.

behaviors.name: User will see a helpful message when Inbox or a list has no tasks
behaviors.expected: An empty Inbox says "Inbox is empty" and an empty list says "No tasks in <list>", each with what to do next.

behaviors.name: User will see an "All done here" message when every task in a view is completed
behaviors.expected: If all tasks in the view are completed and hidden, the view says "All done here" and tells the user to turn on "Show completed".

entities.name: Browse All Tasks
entities.summary: See every task from every list in one place.
entities.description: All Tasks shows every task, open ones first by due date, with finished tasks after them.

behaviors.name: User can see every task from every list in All Tasks
behaviors.expected: All Tasks lists tasks from Inbox and every custom list together.

behaviors.name: User will see open tasks ordered by due date, with undated tasks last
behaviors.expected: Open tasks are listed earliest due date first, and tasks without a due date follow them.

behaviors.name: User will see completed tasks after all open tasks without having to turn anything on
behaviors.expected: All Tasks always includes completed tasks, listed after the open ones, and offers no "Show completed" switch.

behaviors.name: User will see a helpful message when they have no tasks yet
behaviors.expected: With no tasks, All Tasks says "No tasks yet" and tells the user to use New task to add one.

entities.name: Browse Today and Overdue
entities.summary: See everything due today or already late, across all lists.
entities.description: Today gathers incomplete tasks due today or earlier from every list. Late tasks are marked in words, and the view stays correct when the day changes.

behaviors.name: User can see every incomplete task due today or earlier in Today
behaviors.expected: Today lists incomplete tasks from every list whose due date is today or before.

behaviors.name: User will not see tasks due later, without a due date, or already completed in Today
behaviors.expected: Tasks due after today, tasks with no due date and completed tasks are left out of Today.

behaviors.name: User will see the word "Overdue" next to tasks that are late
behaviors.expected: A task due before today shows "Overdue" beside its due date, so lateness never depends on colour alone; tasks due today do not.

behaviors.name: User will see the oldest overdue tasks first
behaviors.expected: Overdue tasks are listed before tasks due today, earliest due date first.

behaviors.name: User can see which list each task in Today belongs to
behaviors.expected: Each task in Today shows the name of its list.

behaviors.name: User will see a helpful message when nothing is due
behaviors.expected: With nothing due or overdue, Today says "Nothing due today" and explains what will appear there.

behaviors.name: User will see Today update at midnight without reloading the page
behaviors.expected: When the local day changes while Tasky is open, tasks due the previous day become Overdue and tasks due on the new day appear.

behaviors.name: User will see Today update when they come back to the window after the day has changed
behaviors.expected: Returning to the window or tab re-checks the local date, so Today and Overdue are never a day out of date.

behaviors.name: User will see Today follow their device time zone when it changes
behaviors.expected: After the device time zone changes, Today and Overdue use the new local date once the window regains focus.

entities.name: Navigate on Narrow Screens
entities.summary: Reach every view and list on a small screen.
entities.description: Below 720px wide the sidebar collapses behind a Menu button.

behaviors.name: User can open and close the navigation menu on a narrow screen
behaviors.expected: Below 720px wide the sidebar is hidden behind a Menu button that opens and closes it, and every view and list stays reachable.

relationships.description: filterTasks calls isDueTodayOrOverdue to decide Today membership.
Creating a task is carried out by TaskRepository.create, which validates and persists it.
Editing a task is carried out by TaskRepository.update, which validates and persists the change.
Completing and reopening a task call TaskRepository.setCompleted.
Deleting a task calls TaskRepository.remove.
Creating a list is carried out by ListRepository.create, which validates and persists it.
Renaming a list is carried out by ListRepository.rename, which validates and persists the change.
Deleting a list calls ListRepository.remove, which moves its tasks to Inbox.
Moving a task between lists is carried out by TaskRepository.update.
A list must exist before it can be renamed.
A list must exist before it can be deleted.
A task can only be assigned to a list that has been created.
Inbox and list views are selected, filtered and ordered by the filtering logic.
Inbox and list views show only the tasks assigned to them.
All Tasks is ordered by the sorting logic.
Today is selected and ordered by the filtering logic.
Today and Overdue are computed from the local calendar date.
Today can only show tasks that exist, so it depends on tasks being created.
Today relies on the due dates people set or change when editing a task.
Completed tasks drop out of Today.
